title: Swallowtail: Russian Espionage Group Targets Defense Firms in Two NATO Countries
description: The Russian espionage group Swallowtail targeted defense-related organizations in two NATO countries, including a law enforcement agency, a naval shipbuilder, and a military aircraft engine manufacturer. The attackers used malicious Word documents to deploy the Hookedge backdoor and conducted hands-on-keyboard operations. They stole credentials using SSH private keys for persistent tunnels and PowerShell scripts to capture NTLM handshakes. Additionally, they deployed a previously undocumented reflective loader (ld.exe) that decrypts payloads in memory with runtime-supplied keys. The campaign aligns with intelligence collection efforts against European government and defense sectors.
aiSummary: Swallowtail, a Russian espionage group, conducted targeted intrusions against organizations in two NATO member states, focusing on defense and law enforcement sectors. The attackers used malicious Word documents to deliver the Hookedge backdoor. They performed hands-on-keyboard activities, stealing credentials through two methods: deploying SSH private keys to maintain persistent network tunnels and executing PowerShell scripts to capture NTLM authentication handshakes. A novel reflective loader (ld.exe) was used to decrypt payloads in memory dynamically, complicating detection. The operation reflects a broad intelligence-gathering campaign targeting sensitive defense-related information in Europe.
aiImpact: The attackers gained unauthorized persistent access to internal networks of high-value defense and law enforcement targets, enabling credential theft and potential lateral movement. The use of advanced techniques such as reflective loaders and credential harvesting tools increases the difficulty of detection and remediation. The compromise of sensitive information related to naval shipbuilding and military aircraft engine manufacturing poses significant risks to national security and defense capabilities.
